Q1: Should the new `passing_change_erased` guard revert the repair (and keep the editor's change) when the gate run before the repair had zero PR-caused failures but a done-check acceptance test was unmet (`rpg_persist_extra > 0`)? From the code, that is the only case where the guard can fire, and it is the case in run 43517436284.
Choices:
- A: Yes. Revert whenever `pr_caused == 0` before the repair, as the issue says, even if only acceptance tests were unmet. The pre-repair result stays final, so the `PERSIST repair_loop` line and the summary will report `acceptance=unmet`, and reviewers see that the done-check failed. The diagnostic line also logs the pre-repair acceptance state and the extra-unmet count. (RECOMMENDED)
- B: Yes, but only when the unmet acceptance tests are ones the editor's change does not touch (no overlap between the editor-changed files and the unmet test paths). Otherwise keep today's behaviour and let the repair's erasure stand.
- C: No. Revert only when `pr_caused == 0` and `rpg_persist_extra == 0`. Given the loop's entry condition this guard would effectively never fire, so the change would amount to adding the diagnostic line. Run 43517436284 would still have lost the editor's change.
